references.text: The preceding verse in [ref:Luk 17:34|Luke 17:34] describes the same pattern – two together, where one is taken and the other is left behind – but with two in one bed, while verse 35 speaks of two grinding together.

[ref:Matt 24:41|Matthew 24:41] is a parallel to this verse: "Two women will be grinding at the mill; one will be taken and the other left behind." Matthew uses the same image of sudden separation at the coming of the Son of Man.
[ref:Matt 24:40|Matthew 24:40] is the parallel to the preceding verse and, together with verse 41, describes the unexpected separation when the Son of Man comes.

In [ref:2 Mos 11:5|Exodus 11:5], the female slave grinding at the mill is mentioned as a picture of the most humble in society. Luke uses the same image of women grinding at the mill, which was everyday work in ancient times.

[ref:Fork 12:3-4|Ecclesiastes 12:3-4] mentions women grinding at the mill, in a context about the end of life and judgment. The image of grinding at the mill was a common part of daily life and is used here as a picture of ordinary tasks that are suddenly interrupted.

[ref:Luk 17:30|Luke 17:30] gives the context for verse 35: "So it will be on the day the Son of Man is revealed." People go about their daily chores – such as grinding grain – and judgment comes suddenly and unexpectedly.

[ref:1 Tess 5:2-3|1 Thessalonians 5:2-3] emphasizes the same theme of the Lord's day coming like a thief in the night, suddenly and unexpectedly, in the midst of daily tasks – which expands on the point in Luke 17:35 about the unexpected separation.
